discrepancies.evidence: crew-runs/g2-implementer-attempt-2.stdout.txt contains only 'Execution error'. g2-implement-rework/plan.json shows m0-m4 complete and m5-result in-progress. g2-implement-rework/m4-full-suite.txt records 3196 passed / 5 skipped / 0 failed. crew-handoffs/g2-implementer-rework-result.md was never written. The registry entry was reconstructed from those artifacts by commander leg 3 and marked abandoned. The successor's write-up was then independently verified: the g2 rework-2 reviewer confirmed every figure labelled MEASURED reproduces in its own hands, every figure labelled RECONSTRUCTED is faithful to its source file, and nothing reconstructed was quietly promoted to first-hand evidence. It also verified at source the successor's claim that rework 1 had an unfinished criterion -- plan.json records m5-result in-progress with both postconditions false. The reconstruct-and-label pattern survived adversarial review.
discrepancies.reason: Recovered by relaunch rather than repair: the rework-2 handoff asks the successor to write up both reworks as one gate result and to say plainly which half it reconstructed from a dead crew's artifacts rather than measured itself. Worth the replanner's attention as a pattern, not this lane's to fix.

discrepancies.signal: Two handoffs on this lane told their crews that .agent-work/ is gitignored and that artifacts under it are intentionally absent from the tracked diff. It is not ignored -- git check-ignore exits 1 -- and this lane's .agent-work/ tree is committed.
discrepancies.affects: The Deliverable Path Check section of the implementer and reviewer handoff templates, which asks for a Committed/Local-only classification and is where the confusion landed.
discrepancies.evidence: git check-ignore .agent-work/cleanup-f-derive-worktree/crew-handoffs/g2-implementer-rework2-result.md exits 1 (not ignored). The lane's own .agent-work/ files appear in git status as untracked-then-committed, e.g. across 52df9e8f. The g2 reviewer-rework handoff and the g3 implementer handoff both carry the false claim.
discrepancies.reason: Untracked was read as ignored. Harmless here -- nothing was lost -- but it teaches a reviewer to expect an artifact to be absent from the diff when it should in fact be committed. Corrected in the g2 rework-2 handoff, which states the correction explicitly rather than silently fixing it.

discrepancies.signal: SessionStart's scan-bind writes a binding for an unbound session onto the single active-leased spine it finds, which is how six crews on this lane were handed their parent Commander's gate
discrepancies.affects: scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py's decide_session_start scan-bind path (_scan_active_spine), and every crew dispatched through run_crew.py under a parent that holds a live engine lease.
discrepancies.evidence: Returned by the g3 implementer and observed live in its own session: a run_crew.py-launched crew has its own session_id and no binding, so decide_session_start falls through to _scan_active_spine, finds exactly one active-leased spine -- its parent's -- and writes a binding for it, after which the crew's own Stop is answered with the parent's execute gate. Binding-key provenance cannot reach it because there is no binding key yet at scan time; the discriminator would have to be the engine lease's owner.
discrepancies.reason: This is the mechanism behind the failure the g3 Protected Intent describes, and g3's fix genuinely cannot reach it -- by provenance the scan-written binding IS the crew's. It touches the scan-bind path rather than the two call sites g3 owned, and changing it needs an authority decision. Recorded as a triage candidate for the return, not filed.

discrepancies.signal: tests/test_code_map.py::MapTreeFreshnessTests is sensitive to the checkout directory name, so any isolated-clone baseline taken outside a directory named constellation-skills reports a false red
discrepancies.affects: Any baseline measurement taken in a fresh clone -- Commander gate closes, Admiral adjudication, and the regression floor a reviewer reproduces.
discrepancies.evidence: main at 17c2cee5 cloned to /tmp/lanef-main-baseline-4 measured 1 failed / 3170 passed / 7 skipped; the same commit cloned to a directory named constellation-skills measured 3171 / 7 / 0. The diff is the map's title line -- '# lanef-main-baseline-4 map' against '# constellation-skills map' -- in an otherwise byte-identical 29k file.
discrepancies.reason: Costs a full suite re-run to anyone who takes a baseline the obvious way, and reads as a real regression until you look at the assertion. Recorded so the next lane names its clone directory rather than rediscovering this.

discrepancies.signal: The g3 handoff's Wiring Grep demanded zero repo-wide references to worktree_from_spine_path, which is not achievable and should not be
discrepancies.affects: The Wiring Grep section of the implementer handoff template as this lane filled it, and any check whose scope is stated more broadly than the Close Criteria it is meant to serve.
discrepancies.evidence: The implementer measured two surviving references outside its allowed scope -- tests/test_worktree_derivation.py's header (which it was forbidden to edit, and which is where the accurate account of the deletion lives) and tests/test_spine_origin_isolation.py's docstring -- and both are TRUE prose recording the deletion rather than stale claims. The same handoff's Close Criteria stated the check correctly, scoped to the two files, and that form was satisfied at 0/0.
discrepancies.reason: A Commander-authored check contradicted its own Close Criteria in the same document. It cost nothing because the implementer measured rather than obeyed, but a less careful crew would have been driven outside its scope to satisfy it. Feeds the feedback step.

discrepancies.signal: A close criterion mandating a non-Test* class name is unsatisfiable-in-silence in a repo that ships no pytest config
discrepancies.affects: The gN-implement gate imperative's close-criteria wording where it mandates a test class name, and the targeted-check design that reads a zero-collected selector as red.
discrepancies.evidence: The gate required the new tests in a class named OwnershipIsBindingKeyNotWorktree. With no pytest config in this repo, a plain class of that name is not collected at all -- the selector would report success while collecting zero. It works only because the implementer made it subclass unittest.TestCase, which the gate never said.
discrepancies.reason: The gate's targeted check was designed to be red on an empty diff and green after; a silently-zero-collected class would read as still-red rather than as a defect, so the failure mode is confusing rather than dangerous. Worth stating in the criterion next time. Feeds the feedback step.

discrepancies.signal: g3's first pass fixed the ownership defect at decide_stop and introduced the SAME defect class at decide_session_start, the sibling call site the gate also owned
discrepancies.affects: scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py decide_session_start's entry selection, and the gate's own recorded decision about what replaces the skip at each call site.
discrepancies.evidence: Independent reviewer BLOCK, reproduced by the Commander with the reviewer's own constructed-payload harness: with a crew in ANOTHER worktree claimed first, a parent's SessionStart resumes from PARENT-MARKER before the change and CREW-MARKER after it -- the deleted tree test was getting that case right. A session with no binding of its own newly resumes from a crew's entry. Writing the parent's key first flips the answer back, which proves selection is dict order and not ownership. The premise that failed is stated in the shipped comment: every entry in the merged view was claimed by THIS session 'under a per-agent key of its own' -- but session_view merges every sid#<agent_id> key and Agent-tool subagents share the parent's session_id, so another AGENT's key is in that view by construction.
discrepancies.reason: Being repaired in g3 rework 1 rather than carried, so it will not block exit once closed. Recorded because the shape is the lane's most instructive: a gate that removes a broken guard inherits every decision the guard was accidentally making, and the sibling site's replacement was argued in prose rather than measured. The reviewer's counter-formulation -- blocking is a spine property at both sites, selection is a binding-key property at both sites -- is the open decision this gate hands up.

discrepancies.signal: An implementer-authored differential harness pinned its BEFORE arm with `git rev-parse HEAD`, so it silently inverted into comparing the change against itself the moment the change was committed
discrepancies.affects: crew-handoffs/g3-implement/m4_differential.py, and any crew-built before/after instrument a later role is told to re-run as verification.
discrepancies.evidence: The harness's docstring names a pinned pre-change base while line 23 reads HEAD at runtime. It was honest at authoring time only. Re-run by the reviewer after the commit, it printed BEFORE (ca577709) and returned 26 identical rows -- including the three rows the review criterion asks a reviewer to spot-check, which came back BEFORE BLOCK / AFTER BLOCK, the exact inverse of the truth, reading as confirmation. The reviewer caught it only because it had already built its own differential and held a contradicting number.
discrepancies.reason: A check that cannot fail is indistinguishable from one that passed, and this one degraded from honest to inverted with no edit and no error. The durable lesson is an ordering one the reviewer named: a verifier should build its own instrument BEFORE running the one the implementer shipped. Feeds the feedback step.

discrepancies.signal: g3 rework 1's correct fix for the sibling call site fed a pre-existing write path, and the binding it wrote then defeated the Stop path's foreign-owner withholding -- reproducing #549 in the relaxing direction, in the change whose purpose is to end it
discrepancies.affects: scripts/hooks/spine_rail.py decide_session_start's bind-on-resume branch, and the general shape of removing a guard that was accidentally gating a write.
discrepancies.evidence: Second independent reviewer BLOCK, reproduced by the Commander with the reviewer's three-arm harness. Before rework 1, any session that could SEE an entry left the selection loop non-None and never reached the scan-bind block. Ownership-based selection newly routes 'can see entries, owns none' sessions into it, and on exactly one active-leased in-tree spine it writes a binding under the BARE sid -- precisely the key _own_entries reads as OWN. The following Stop is then answered with the crew's gate as its own, leaking the crew's next imperative into both reason and additionalContext. Measured: OLD and BLOCKED arms wrote nothing and rendered foreign-owner with no leak; the rework arm wrote binding[sid]=the crew's spine and leaked. Control row with no SessionStart is clean on all three arms, so the restart is the whole difference. Reachable on this lane's own topology: a crew claims the in-tree spine under sid#agent_id, the parent has no claim of its own, and the parent's session restarts after a compaction.
discrepancies.reason: Being repaired in g3 rework 2 as a condition on the existing branch, so it will not block exit once closed. Recorded because of HOW it evaded detection, which is the transferable part: the Stop path is unchanged per call, so no single-call differential can see it, and every SessionStart test on this gate placed its spines outside the scan's glob so the scan never fired. The defect needs the in-tree topology AND a two-call sequence. Rework 1's own tests asserted _scan_active_spine(proj) == [] before acting -- good discipline against a different failure, and structurally blind to this one. The shipped comment also claimed the site 'withholds rather than guessing' while the code it guarded went on to bind, which is the lane's stale-claim defect class for the fourth time.
